fields.sample_size: qualitative study in the Omusati Region, north-central Namibia: regional and local actor interviews plus focus groups in villages (28 focus-group participants: Enongo 6 men and 4 women, Eenkalashe 3 and 3, Olwaadhiya 6 and 6); number of interviews not extracted
fields.effect_estimate: Since the late-1990s reforms (water point committees under the Directorate of Water Supply and Sanitation Coordination), local actors participate in governance but participation is often tokenistic; insufficient funding undermines it (e.g. water point committee strikes lead to defaulted user payments and closed water points) and gatekeepers can block change; participants in some villages see no benefit or incentive in taking part in decisions. Decentralisation is ineffective when government does not provide the resources and capacity to local actors. Qualitative; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: qualitative case study (interviews and village focus groups in one region)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (interviews, focus groups with 28 participants, coding); Results (participation, funding, gatekeepers); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Methods (interviews, focus groups with 28 participants, coding); Results (participation, funding, gatekeepers); Conclusion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative study of decentralised water governance in Omusati Region, Namibia (focus groups with 28 villagers plus actor interviews), read in full text 2026-10-04. Participation is often tokenistic; under-funded water point committees and strikes disrupt payment and service; capacity support needed. One region.
